title: spec review: S2g contracts: per-role machine-validated worker output contracts and a bounded recovery ladder (deterministic repair, schema-repair resume, rerun) in shadow (P17, P18)
spec:
Create orchestrator/contracts.py. SCHEMAS per role: scout {findings: [{claim, location, confidence}], unresolved: [str], summary}, execute {summary, files_changed: [str], commits: [str], tests_run: [str], test_result: pass|fail|not_run, unresolved: [str]}, review and spec_review {verdict: approve|request_changes, findings: [{severity: high|medium|low, location, text}], required_changes: [str], risks: [str]}, challenge {claim, evidence: [str], agreement: agree|disagree|partial, confidence}, plus confidence and provenance on all (bus.post_result defaults). validate(role, result) -> {"ok": bool, "errors": [str], "repaired": dict|None}: deterministic repair first (key aliases such as files/changed_files, string-to-list coercions, verdict synonyms approve/approved/LGTM, confidence strings to float, drop unknown keys into extra); ok when the repaired result satisfies the schema. Recovery ladder in spawn.py at the point where extract_json runs on the worker output: 1 validate; 2 if not ok and [contracts].mode is active: one bounded schema-repair request resumed on the same session or thread (claude --resume session_id or codex resume) asking for only the JSON object for this role's schema, budget [contracts].repair_budget_usd (default 0.5) and one attempt; log a runs row role output_repair with tokens; 3 if still not ok, fall through to today's behaviour (review roles fail with no parseable verdict, others keep the raw result). [contracts].mode = "shadow" (dated comment): validate and record a decision_log row kind output_contract (add to KINDS) with role, ok, errors, repaired_keys, selected = accept|repair|rerun (shadow: what active would do), but never resume or change the stored result. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/13-output-contracts.md with the schemas and the shadow validation rate measured over the real task results on this repository (bus tasks with results, per role: ok, repairable, invalid).
Spec review T-1091 folded in: (1) Validation runs at every result-posting point, not only where extract_json runs: spawn.run_worker's non-execute branch, spawn's Claude-fallback execute branch, and executor.post_tool_result for Codex execute results (scope adds orchestrator/executor.py); each validates the dict it is about to post against the role schema, applies deterministic repair, records the decision_log row, and in active mode may use the bounded repair request where a session or thread exists. (2) The mode is a promotion feature: add contracts to promotion.FEATURES (scope adds orchestrator/promotion.py and tests/test_promotion.py) with criteria (30 shadow rows, repair success rate, no rise in failed results) and read it through promotion.mode("contracts"), never pool.cfg directly. (3) Interface contract, fixed here and mirrored into plan.md: contracts.SCHEMAS: dict role -> schema (required keys with types, optional keys, enums); contracts.validate(role, result) -> {ok: bool, errors: [str], repaired: dict | None}; contracts.repair(role, result) -> dict (deterministic, idempotent); contracts.recover(role, result, *, session=None, thread=None, budget_usd) -> {result, repaired_by: none|deterministic|model, tokens} used only in active mode.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_output_contract_active_repair_resume_once_within_budget (patched resume returns valid JSON; runs row output_repair written)

risks.issue: contracts.SCHEMAS.review = {verdict, findings:[{severity,location,text}], required_changes, risks} does not match what workers are actually told to emit here: {verdict, comments:[{path,line,issue,severity}]}. There is no findings/required_changes/risks field in the real prompt, and comments' shape (path+line, issue) differs from findings' (location, text). Deterministic repair (key aliases, list coercions) cannot bridge a comments->findings restructuring. Every real review result will validate as invalid/repairable, which misrepresents the shadow measurement as 'drift' when it is really a schema-vs-prompt mismatch.

Same schema is reused for spec_review, but this prompt (used to generate this very review) asks for {verdict, risks:[{path,issue,severity,line}], suggested_spec_changes}. 'risks' here is a list of objects; the spec's schema defines risks as [str]. required_changes/findings do not exist in this prompt at all.

Spec's challenge schema is {claim, evidence:[str], agreement: agree|disagree|partial, confidence}. The actual prompt asks for {verdict: confirmed|refuted|uncertain, evidence:[path:line], note}. There is no 'agreement' enum or 'claim' output field, and confirmed/refuted/uncertain is not a synonym set for agree/disagree/partial that deterministic repair's verdict-synonym table (approve/approved/LGTM) would plausibly cover.

Spec's scout schema is {findings:[{claim,location,confidence}], unresolved, summary}. Actual prompt asks for {findings:[{claim,evidence:[path:line],confidence,provenance}], open_questions, suggested_next, blocked} with no 'summary' or 'unresolved' key and per-finding 'provenance' (needed because scouts cite mixed repo/web/ticket sources) that the spec pushes to a single top-level provenance default instead, losing per-claim provenance.

Spec's execute schema requires files_changed:[str], commits:[str], tests_run:[str], test_result. The only two places execute results are actually posted are this function (posted = {summary, commit (singular string, not a list), executed_by, provenance, usage, thread, rounds}) and spawn.py's Claude-fallback branch (summary, executed_by, review). Neither ever populates files_changed, commits, tests_run or test_result, so role=execute will validate as invalid for effectively 100% of historical and future results, not because of worker drift but because the schema names fields nothing in the codebase produces.
Companion evidence for the executor.py finding: the Claude-fallback execute post here has an even smaller, differently-shaped result than the proposed execute schema.

record() has no defaults for candidates, hard_constraints, deterministic or reason. The spec only names role, ok, errors, repaired_keys, selected for the new output_contract row and leaves these required fields unspecified, so the executor has to invent semantics (e.g. what counts as a 'candidate' for a validation outcome) that a reviewer has no basis to check for consistency with existing kinds.

collect() is a hand-dispatched if/elif per feature name with a bare {"n":0} fallback for anything unhandled; scope/acceptance only add a FEATURES entry and test_contracts_feature_registered, never a collect() branch for 'contracts'. The spec's prose criteria (30 shadow rows, repair success rate, no rise in failed results) therefore has no evidence path wired and promotion.report() will show n=0 for this feature indefinitely unless a later task adds a collect() branch that reads decision_log kind=output_contract rows.

suggested_spec_changes: Derive contracts.SCHEMAS from the JSON actually requested in .orchestrator/prompts/{scout,review,spec-review,challenge}.md and from what executor.py/spawn.py actually post for execute, not from an idealized shape; treat the prompt files as the source of truth for role output shape (or fold updating them into this task's scope if the new field names are wanted going forward).

Make execute's files_changed/commits/tests_run/test_result optional-with-unknown-default (or add a deterministic repair step that derives them from git diff/log at post time) so the schema doesn't declare fields no code path ever fills.
Pin the exact decision_log.record() call for the output_contract row (candidates=, hard_constraints=, deterministic=, reason=) in the spec so all reviewers/executors use the same convention.

Either drop the promotion criteria language (30 shadow rows, repair success rate, no rise in failed results) from this task's spec since it isn't wired, or add scope/acceptance for a promotion.collect() 'contracts' branch that reads decision_log kind=output_contract rows so the criteria are actually measurable.
